In this context, an "author" refers to the person who created a literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic work. This is evident from sections (1) and (3) of subsection 127, which mention:

* "(1) Where a name purporting to be that of the author of a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work appeared on copies of the work as published..."
* "...the person whose name so appeared, if it was his or her true name or a name by which he or she was commonly known, shall... be presumed to be the author of the work..."

Additionally, in section (b) of another excerpt, an "author" is mentioned as someone who can be represented or protected under the law of another country.

It's worth noting that this definition seems to align with general intellectual property and copyright terminology. An author is typically considered the person who creates original content, such as a writer of a book, composer of music, or painter of artwork.
